summary: Build self-serve Slack namespace with just-in-time RBAC, lifecycle hooks and automated archival
description:
Issue summary:
Request to create a self-service Slack namespace (provisioning gateway) that allows pod leads to create partner and project channels with just-in-time RBAC, preflight data-classification checks, templated channel settings, and automated lifecycle hooks for archival and audit export.

Impact:
Current channel provisioning is manual and centralized. This causes delays for partner work, inconsistent channel metadata, and an accumulation of stale channels that complicate audits and increases noise. A self-serve gateway will speed onboarding, reduce manual admin load, and enforce guardrails.

Desired outcome:
- A lightweight provisioning service (Slack app + automation) accessible via a Jira / Confluence form and Slack command.
- RBAC is granted via short-lived ephemeral grants tied to Okta group approvals (JIT: max 7 days) with automatic revocation.
- Channel templates (private/public, retention, pinned resources, on-call rotas) selectable at creation.
- Lifecycle hooks: reminder at 30/90/180 days, optional archival workflow with archive reason + export to Confluence, and automatic archival for channels flagged as inactive for 240 days.
- Audit events emitted to central audit log (Confluence page and ingestion hook) and optional export to customer-compliant S3 bucket for partner channels.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Pod lead can create a channel via /provision-channel command or a Confluence form and receive JIT RBAC for collaborators.
2) Template selection applies channel topic, purpose, retention, and pinned resources.
3) Channel lifecycle events appear in audit log and produce a Confluence export summary on archival.
4) Automation includes an opt-out flow for channels that require extended retention and sets a manual approval path.

Steps to reproduce (how a pod lead would use it):
1) Run /provision-channel in #pilot-ops with parameters: template=partner-private, collaborators=@alice,@bob, retention=90d.
2) System creates private channel, applies topic/purpose, pins the onboarding doc, and posts a creation summary.
3) Okta approval flow triggers ephemeral membership grants for external collaborators for 7 days.
4) 30/90/180 day reminders posted; no response after 240 days triggers archival job and Confluence export.

Risks & constraints:
- Okta JIT integration work required with Security review for ephemeral guest access.
- Exporting partner data requires consent and potential S3 bucket tenancy for compliance.
- Need to avoid flooding #support with automation messages; rate-limit notifications.

Stakeholders:
- Requester: Product Partnerships (Aisha Patel)
- Security: Priya Singh (review RBAC / guest access)
- Platform/Infra: Connor Miller (assignee)
- Legal/Compliance: Marcos Diaz (export and retention policy)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) User runs /provision-channel with template and collaborators. 2) Provisioning service creates channel and applies settings. 3) JIT RBAC issues ephemeral Okta guest link for external users. 4) Lifecycle reminders post and archival triggers after 240 days of inactivity.
investigation_notes:
Initial spike completed 2026-03-11. Prototype Slack app can create channels and set topic/purpose. Okta team confirmed API for JIT group membership exists but requires scoped service account and approval from Security. Performance: creating channels via Slack API within rate limits is feasible; rate-limiting strategy: batch notifications and exponential backoff.
Open questions: whether to store audit exports in central S3 (Platform-managed) vs tenant-specific buckets for partner channels. Need Legal sign-off on retention lengths for partner PII.
Links:
- Slack prototype repo: github.com/redwood/provisioning-slack-app (PR TBD)

Priya Singh (2026-03-11): Security OK in principle but need threat model and service account constraints before enabling ephemeral guest provisioning.
Marcos Diaz (2026-03-12): Legal requires opt-in consent flow for exporting partner messages; propose flagging partner channels at creation so export runs only when consent true.
Connor Miller (2026-03-12): Next steps: open PR for Slack app with feature flags (+ Confluence export job). Scheduling 2-hour review with Security on 2026-03-18.
resolution: IN PROGRESS - prototype validated for basic channel creation and templating. Security backlog item opened for Okta JIT service account. Legal requested opt-in export flag; design adjusted to include consent checkbox in the Confluence form. Follow-ups: 1) Security review (2026-03-18), 2) implement export S3 scoping and consent UI (owner: Marcos Diaz), 3) rate-limit and alert tuning (owner: Connor Miller).
resolution_notes: Prototype turned into feature branch. Security review scheduled. Will not enable JIT guest provisioning in prod until Security and Legal sign-off and scoped service account are in place. Aim to land MVP behind feature flag by end of Q2 2026.
acceptance_criteria: Self-serve channel creation via Slack command or Confluence form
JIT RBAC grants for external collaborators (7-day ephemeral) with automatic revocation
Lifecycle reminders and automated archival after inactivity threshold
Export produces Confluence summary and optional S3 export when consented
